ChatCitation.description:
One `@cite[...]` entry from the answer's evidence block.

PDF citations carry `page` (and `paper_id` when the quote came from a
supplementary or other paper); code citations carry `file` plus the line
range, `verified` and a SHA-pinned `github_url` instead. Keys that were
never set are absent from the JSON; `github_url`/`start_line`/`end_line`
can be an explicit null.
ChatCitation.title: ChatCitation

ChatMessageMetadata.description:
UIMessage `metadata` of an assistant turn that never completed:
`interrupted` alone for a stop/disconnect, plus `errorText` when the run
failed.
ChatMessageMetadata.title: ChatMessageMetadata

ChatStreamSchema.description:
Schema-only container that makes the stream's custom types appear in
the OpenAPI document. Never actually served.
ChatStreamSchema.title: ChatStreamSchema

ConversationPage.title: ConversationPage

DataUIPart.description: Data part with dynamic type based on data name.
DataUIPart.title: DataUIPart

DiscoverResult.description:
One search hit, as stored in `discover_searches.results`.

Exa hits carry `summary`; OpenAlex hits carry `cited_by_count`, `source`
and `institutions`. A TypedDict (not a model) so each hit serializes with
only the keys it was stored with.
DiscoverResult.title: DiscoverResult

DocumentSummary.description:

post.description:
Create a NOTE doc attached to a paper. Body content always starts empty;
the user types into the editor right after switching to it.

get.description:
Return the MAIN document for a paper, creating it on first call.

Idempotent: subsequent calls return the same row. The editor uses this on
mount and to reload after a 409 conflict.

delete.description:
Delete a NOTE doc. MAIN docs are protected — returns 400 to keep the
paper's primary writeup from disappearing accidentally.

get.description:
Return a single doc by id (any kind). Used by the editor when it
switches to a NOTE doc — content is what the Milkdown editor hydrates from.

patch.description:
Rename a doc. Title-only here — content updates go through PUT so they
keep the optimistic-locking semantics that the agent relies on.

put.description:
Replace document content, gated by `expected_revision`.

413 if content exceeds the hard size cap.
409 (with `current_revision` and `current_content`) on stale revision so
    the editor can prompt the user to reload without an extra round-trip.
